tasks.gr11-network-topologies-t3: Topic: Network Topologies. Cover network types (LAN — Local Area Network, WAN — Wide Area Network, MAN — Metropolitan Area Network), physical topologies (bus, star, ring, mesh), the characteristics of each topology, advantages and disadvantages (e.g. star: single point of failure at switch; bus: cheap but a cable break affects all nodes; ring: predictable performance; mesh: resilient but expensive), and the concept of a client-server vs peer-to-peer network. Ask Grade 11 learners to identify topologies from diagrams, compare topologies for a given scenario, explain what happens when a node fails in each topology, and distinguish LAN from WAN.
tasks.gr11-protocols-media-t3: Topic: Protocols and Communication Media. Cover the TCP/IP protocol stack, key application-layer protocols (HTTP/HTTPS for web, FTP for file transfer, SMTP for sending email, POP3/IMAP for receiving email, DNS for name resolution), wired media (twisted pair/Ethernet, fibre optic — faster, more secure, less interference), wireless media (Wi-Fi/IEEE 802.11, Bluetooth for short range, 4G/5G for mobile), IP addresses (IPv4 structure, public vs private), and the role of a router and switch. Ask Grade 11 learners to match protocols to their purpose, compare wired and wireless media, explain what DNS does, and identify the correct protocol for a communication scenario.
tasks.gr11-data-processing-t3: Topic: Data Processing and Validation. Cover input validation techniques (range check, type check, presence check, length check, format check), exception handling (try-catch or try-except blocks to prevent crashes), processing arrays (traversal, search, accumulator patterns, counting), combining arrays with file I/O for batch processing, and producing meaningful output (formatted totals, averages, counts). Ask Grade 11 learners to identify the appropriate validation check for a scenario, trace code with exception handling, complete array-processing algorithms, and explain the difference between a syntax error and a runtime exception.
tasks.gr11-social-implications-t3: Topic: Social Implications of Technology. Cover privacy rights and the Protection of Personal Information Act (POPIA) — lawful purpose, data minimisation, consent, data subject rights; types of cybercrime (phishing, identity theft, ransomware, cyberbullying, hacking, piracy); protective measures (strong passwords, 2FA, firewalls, antivirus, VPN, encryption, regular updates); responsible digital communication (netiquette, copyright, plagiarism); and the digital divide. Ask Grade 11 learners to classify a described crime, recommend appropriate security measures for a scenario, explain a POPIA principle, and evaluate the ethical dimensions of a technology use case.
tasks.gr11-database-design-keys-erd-t3: Topic: Database Design: Keys, Relationships and ERDs. Cover data versus information, fields, records and tables, primary, alternate, foreign and composite keys, one-to-many relationships, referential integrity and entity relationship diagrams. Ask Grade 11 learners to name a key, place a foreign key, or say what referential integrity prevents.
tasks.gr11-database-access-code-multi-form-t3: Topic: Using a Database in Code and Multi-Form Programs. Cover connecting to a single-table database by path, a dataset and its current record, moving through records, editing, adding, deleting and posting, multi-form programs, passing values and returning values, and checking with trace tables. Ask Grade 11 learners to complete a loop over the records, say why a change must be posted, or describe how forms work together.
